Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Reauthorization Act: Senate passed S. 4472, to amend the Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Act to reauthorize the provisions of such Act through fiscal year 2031, after agreeing to the committee amendment in the nature of a substitute.

Measures Considered:

AGOA Extension Act--Agreement: Senate continued consideration of the motion to proceed to consideration of H.R. 6500, to extend duty-free treatment provided with respect to imports from certain countries in Africa under the African Growth and Opportunity Act, to extend customs user fees.
Pages S4415–4425

A unanimous-consent agreement was reached providing for further consideration of the motion to proceed to consideration of the bill, post-cloture, at approximately 10:30 a.m., on Wednesday, August 5, 2026; and that if cloture is invoked on the nomination of Erica Schwartz, of Florida, to be Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Senate vote on confirmation of the nomination at 2:15 p.m.
Page S4444

Appointments:

Board of Trustees of the Institute of American Indian and Alaska Native Culture and Arts Development: The Chair, on behalf of the President pro tempore, in accordance with Public Law 99–498, Section 1505(a)(1)(B)(ii), appointed the following Senator to the Board of Trustees of the Institute of American Indian and Alaska Native Culture and Arts Development: Senator Luján.
Page S4425


Modification to the Start of the Submission Period for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Reporting and Recordkeeping Under TSCA 8(a)(7)--Agreement: A unanimous-consent agreement was reached providing that notwithstanding Rule XXII, Senator Whitehouse, or his designee, be authorized to return the Senate to legislative session for the purpose of making a motion to proceed to consideration of S.J. Adjournment: Senate convened at 10:01 a.m. and adjourned at 10:21 p.m., until 10:30 a.m. on Wednesday, August 5, 2026. (For Senate's program, see the remarks of the Majority Leader in today's Record on page S4444.)

Committee Meetings

(Committees not listed did not meet)

REALITY OF MEDICAID

Committee on the Budget: Committee concluded a hearing to examine the reality of Medicaid, after receiving testimony from Brian C. Blase, Paragon Health Institute, Arlington, Virginia; Jonathan Ingram, Foundation for Government Accountability, Naples, Florida; and Andy Schneider, Georgetown University McCourt School of Public Policy, Washington D.C.

HEALTH CARE WITH BIOTECHNOLOGY

Committee on Finance: Subcommittee on Health Care concluded a hearing to examine building a resilient health care future with biotechnology, after receiving testimony from Michelle Rozo, Vice Chair, National Security Commission on Emerging Biotechnology (NSCEB); Alan D. Palkowitz, Indiana Biosciences Research Institute, Indianapolis; Vera P. Luther, Infectious Diseases Society of America, Lebanon, New Hampshire; and Kevin Outterson, Boston University School of Law, Boston, Massachusetts.

BUSINESS MEETING

Committee on the Judiciary: Committee ordered favorably reported the nomination of Todd Blanche, of Florida, to be Attorney General.

AI SURVEILLANCE PRICING

Committee on the Judiciary: Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism concluded a hearing to examine data and profit, focusing on the consumer cost of AI surveillance pricing, after receiving testimony from Hillary Caron, United Food and Commercial Workers International Union, Lee A. Hepner, American Economic Liberties Project, and Lindsay Owens, Groundwork Collaborative, all of Washington, D.C.; Robert B. Hedges, Jr., Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Oxford, New Hampshire; and Z. John Zhang, University of Pennsylvania Wharton School, Philadelphia.

INTELLIGENCE

Select Committee on Intelligence: Committee held closed hearings on intelligence matters, receiving testimony from officials of the intelligence community.

Committee recessed subject to the call.

Next Meeting of the
SENATE

10:30 a.m., Wednesday, August 5

Senate Chamber

Program for Wednesday: Senate will continue consideration of the motion to proceed to consideration of H.R. 6500, AGOA Extension Act (legislative vehicle for the continuing resolution), post-cloture.

Senate will vote on the motion to invoke cloture on the nomination of Erica Schwartz, of Florida, to be Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, at 11:30 a.m. If cloture is invoked, Senate will vote on confirmation of the nomination at 2:15 p.m.

Following disposition of the nomination of Erica Schwartz, Senate will vote on the motion to invoke cloture on the en bloc nominations, provided under the provisions of S. Res. 817 (119th Congress).

If Senator Whitehouse or his designee makes a motion to proceed to consideration of S.J. Res. 187, Modification to the Start of the Submission Period for Perfluoroalkyl and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Reporting and Recordkeeping Under TSCA 8(a)(7), Senate will vote on the motion to proceed during Wednesday's session of the Senate.
